sentences.en: And so today, we are going to talk about good-bad movies.

sentences.en: I'm joined in my good-bad movie deep dive by my colleague, Maya Salam, who, for the last year, has been writing a column about good-bad movies for The Times.
sentences.zh: 和我一起深入探讨“又好又烂”电影的是我的同事玛雅·萨拉姆，在过去的一年里，她一直在为《时报》撰写关于“又好又烂”电影的专栏。

sentences.en: And later in this episode, I will gather a couple other of my esteemed colleagues, Taffy Brodesser-Akner and Gilbert Cruz, to tell me about their must-see good-bad movies.

sentences.en: It's Sunday, September 13th.
sentences.zh: 今天是9月13日，星期日。

sentences.en: Maya Salam, welcome to the Sunday Daily.
sentences.zh: 玛雅·萨拉姆，欢迎来到星期日《每日新闻》。

sentences.en: Thank you so much, Rachel.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢，雷切尔。

sentences.en: I'm thrilled to be here.
sentences.zh: 我很兴奋能来到这里。

sentences.en: So, Maya, you have been working on this project, which seems very fun, about good-bad movies.
sentences.zh: 所以，玛雅，你一直在进行这个关于“又好又烂”电影的项目，听起来非常有趣。

sentences.en: You have been naming good-bad movies.
sentences.zh: 你一直在列举“又好又烂”的电影。

sentences.en: You've been dissecting them.
sentences.zh: 你一直在剖析它们。

sentences.en: You've been trying to figure out the specific ingredients that make a good-bad movie so beloved.
sentences.zh: 你一直在试图找出让一部“又好又烂”的电影如此受人喜爱的具体成分。

sentences.en: And I want to talk about all of those ingredients, but first, let's define what we are talking about.
sentences.zh: 我想聊聊所有这些成分，但首先，让我们定义一下我们在谈论什么。

sentences.en: What do we mean when we say good-bad movie?
sentences.zh: 当我们说“又好又烂”的电影时，我们是什么意思？

sentences.en: Well, first, let me say that everyone has their own rubric, their own parameters, their own boxes that need to be checked for a good-bad movie.
sentences.zh: 嗯，首先，我想说每个人都有自己的准则、自己的参数、自己的标准，来衡量一部“又好又烂”的电影。

sentences.en: So, there's the way that I define it for the series, but there are no wrong answers, really.
sentences.zh: 所以，这是我为这个系列所下的定义，但真的没有错误的答案。

sentences.en: And for me, it's a movie that has at least one element, but usually more, that are completely over-the-top, are completely absurd, and the movie must be, above all else,
sentences.zh: 对我而言，这是一部至少包含一个、但通常包含更多完全夸张、完全荒谬元素的电影，而且最重要的是，这部电影必须

sentences.en: highly watchable, highly re-watchable.
sentences.zh: 极具观看价值，极具重温价值。

sentences.en: And while it may not be great cinema, so to speak, they are movies that are infectious, are beloved, that people return to again and again,
sentences.zh: 虽然它可能算不上什么伟大的电影艺术，但它们是那种具有感染力、深受喜爱、人们会一遍又一遍重温的电影，

sentences.en: and often have a lot of feelings and memories tied up with them.
sentences.zh: 而且通常与它们绑定了许多情感和记忆。

sentences.en: Let's talk about an example of a good-bad movie.
sentences.zh: 让我们来谈谈“又好又烂”电影的一个例子。

sentences.en: You have written about all different sorts of good-bad movies.
sentences.zh: 你写过各种各样的“又好又烂”的电影。

sentences.zh: 我们挑一部吧，玛雅。

sentences.en: So, okay, I know this movie.
sentences.zh: 好吧，我知道这部电影。

sentences.en: For the uninitiated, for people that did not have the pleasure of seeing this film, tell us a little bit more about why it might qualify as a good-bad movie.
sentences.zh: 对于外行人来说，对于没有荣幸看过这部电影的人，请跟我们多讲讲为什么它有资格被称为“又好又烂”的电影。

sentences.en: Some of the things that make Volcano a good-bad movie are the fact that the main cast, while other people are catching fire, exploding, melting before our eyes,
sentences.zh: 让《火山爆发》成为一部“又好又烂”电影的因素之一，是当其他人在我们眼前着火、爆炸、融化时，主角阵容

sentences.zh: 却几乎连汗都不出一滴。

sentences.en: Even though they are the closest to the lava, Anne Heche and Tommy Lee Jones are more or less just fine, even when they're hanging just mere feet above a lava flow.
sentences.zh: 尽管他们离熔岩最近，但安妮·海切和汤米·李·琼斯基本上安然无恙，甚至当他们悬挂在离熔岩流只有几英尺高的地方时也是如此。

sentences.en: It's things like this that are good-bad gold, honestly.
sentences.zh: 老实说，正是诸如此类的事情才是“又好又烂”电影的黄金精华。

sentences.en: Okay, so it's very watchable.
sentences.zh: 好吧，所以它极具观看性。

sentences.en: It's highly unrealistic.
sentences.zh: 它极不真实。

sentences.en: What makes it bad?
sentences.zh: 是什么让它变烂的？

sentences.en: What makes up the bad part of the good-bad of Volcano?
sentences.zh: 是什么构成了《火山爆发》中“烂”的那一部分？

sentences.en: Yeah, I usually try to kind of identify one element in all these movies that really is bad.
sentences.zh: 是的，我通常试图在所有这些电影中找出一种确实很烂的元素。

sentences.en: And in Volcano, that is the fact that they try to tie in this metaphor of racial tension in Los Angeles in the 1990s, make the volcano a metaphor for that.
sentences.zh: 在《火山爆发》中，那就是他们试图将20世纪90年代洛杉矶种族紧张局势的隐喻融入其中，把火山比作这种隐喻。

sentences.en: There's a mention of Rodney King.
sentences.zh: 这里提到了罗德尼·金。

sentences.en: There's a child who is, at the end, while everyone is covered in ash, realizes that he's, you know, colorblind because everyone's the same color.
sentences.zh: 最后，当每个人都覆盖着火山灰时，有一个孩子意识到，你知道的，他是色盲，因为每个人都是同一个颜色。

sentences.en: Extremely cringey.

sentences.en: Oof.

sentences.en: Definitely not necessary to the plot.
sentences.zh: 对剧情来说绝对没有必要。

sentences.en: So basically, this film decided it had to be about more than just a volcano erupting in Los Angeles, and in your estimation, did not pull that off particularly well.
sentences.zh: 所以基本上，这部电影决定不仅要讲洛杉矶火山爆发的故事，而且在你的估计中，这一点并没有处理得特别好。

sentences.en: Exactly that.
sentences.zh: 正是如此。

sentences.en: The elephant in the room here, I feel like, is also the fact that, you know, who gets to define what is good?
sentences.zh: 我觉得，这里显而易见的问题还在于，你知道的，谁来定义什么是好的？

sentences.en: If a movie is broadly popular, does that not mean that it's good?
sentences.zh: 如果一部电影广受欢迎，难道不就意味着它是好的吗？

sentences.en: Is it only good if it wins an Oscar?
sentences.zh: 难道只有赢得奥斯卡奖的才是好电影吗？

sentences.en: Is it only good if the critics—I mean, this is like an argument as old as time a little bit.
sentences.zh: 难道只有评论家——我的意思是，这就像是一个古老得有点过时的争论。

sentences.en: So it's sort of interesting to think about who gets to define what even makes a movie good to begin with.
sentences.zh: 所以思考一下究竟是谁来定义是什么让一部电影一开始就成为好电影，是一件挺有意思的事。

sentences.en: I think what I love about these choices and getting to kind of elevate these movies is because when we talk about a lot of movies that are obviously wonderful cinema, great films,
sentences.zh: 我想我喜欢这些选择以及能够提升这些电影的原因是，当我们谈论许多显然是精彩电影艺术、伟大电影的影片时，

sentences.en: you know, they get a lot of attention, and as they should.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，它们得到了很多关注，这是它们应得的。

sentences.en: And then, you know, we give a lot of attention to movies that flop epically.
sentences.zh: 然后，你知道的，我们给予那些惨败的电影很多关注。

sentences.en: But there's this really rich middle, and this series kind of does service to that middle, because whether these movies were blockbusters, and some of them were,
sentences.zh: 但这里有一个非常丰富的中间地带，这个系列某种程度上服务于这个中间地带，因为无论这些电影是否是轰动一时的热门大片——其中一些确实是，

sentences.en: and whether they were complete flops in every sense of the word, they've managed to remain relevant.
sentences.zh: 也无论它们在各个意义上是彻底的惨败，它们都设法保持了相关性。

sentences.en: And a lot of them have, like, universal name recognition.
sentences.zh: 而且它们中的许多都具有普遍的知名度。

sentences.en: So even if you've never watched them, you're aware of it.
sentences.zh: 所以即使你从未看过它们，你也知道它们的存在。

sentences.en: They've really worked their way into the pop culture zeitgeiSt.
sentences.zh: 它们真的已经融入了流行文化的时代精神中。

sentences.en: And also, people still want to talk about them, right?
sentences.zh: 而且，人们仍然想谈论它们，对吧？

sentences.en: I have to confess to you, when we were even discussing your series here on The Daily, inevitably, every single discussion we had turned into producers, editors, hosts.
sentences.zh: 我不得不向你坦白，当我们甚至在《每日新闻》上讨论你的这个系列时，我们进行的每一次讨论都不可避免地变成了制片人、编辑、主持人的讨论。

sentences.en: Everybody wanted to talk about their favorite movie that might not necessarily be considered good, but that they loved.
sentences.zh: 每个人都想谈论他们最喜欢的电影，这些电影可能不一定被认为是好的，但他们就是很喜欢。

sentences.en: I wonder what you make of that, that reaction that your series has instilled.
sentences.zh: 我想知道你对你的系列所引发的这种反应作何感想。

sentences.en: I love that question, and I love that this has done that.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢这个问题，我也很高兴它达到了这样的效果。

sentences.en: You know, we're living in a time where there's really no monoculture,
sentences.zh: 你知道的，我们生活在一个实际上没有单一主流文化的时代，

sentences.en: so there is something really nostalgic and satisfying about getting to have sort of these water cooler conversations that were common once upon a time.
sentences.zh: 所以能够进行那种曾经司空见惯的茶水间闲聊，确实有一种非常怀旧和满足的感觉。

sentences.en: How often these days do we talk to somebody and they ask, have you seen the show?
sentences.zh: 现在我们跟人聊天时，对方问“你看过这个节目吗”的频率有多高？

sentences.en: Have you seen this film?
sentences.zh: 你看过这部电影吗？

sentences.en: And not only haven't you seen it, you maybe have never even heard of it.
sentences.zh: 不仅没看过，你甚至可能听都没听说过。

sentences.en: You know, especially, even me and people at our desk who live and breathe television and film encounter that.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，尤其是，甚至我和我们办公室那些以电视和电影为生的人也会遇到这种情况。

sentences.en: And that really is a sign of how our pop culture consumption has fragmented.
sentences.zh: 这确实表明了我们的流行文化消费是如何碎片化的。

sentences.en: But I think with these good, bad movies, I think what they are is the opportunity to banter, the opportunity to have these debates, low-stakes debates,
sentences.zh: 但我认为对于这些所谓的“雷片好片”，它们提供的是一个开玩笑的机会，一个进行这种低风险辩论的机会，

sentences.en: because these movies are low-stakes.
sentences.zh: 因为这些电影本来就没什么大不了的。

sentences.en: And it is fun to get the opportunity to do that.
sentences.zh: 有机会做这件事其实挺有意思的。

sentences.en: And it's also fun to say, why don't you fight me on it a little bit?
sentences.zh: 而且这样也挺好玩的：为什么不稍微跟我争论一下呢？

sentences.en: Why don't we have this push and pull for something that doesn't really matter all that much?
sentences.zh: 为什么我们不能为一件其实没那么重要的事情争论一番、拉扯一下呢？

sentences.en: Okay, I really want to lean into that idea that we should all be having sort of low-stakes fights with other people, that somehow that is edifying to our souls.
sentences.zh: 好吧，我真的很想深入探讨这样一个观点：我们所有人都应该和别人进行这种无伤大雅的争论，某种程度上这对我们的心灵是有滋养作用的。

sentences.en: So after the break, that's exactly what we're going to do.
sentences.zh: 所以在休息之后，我们将要做的正是这件事。

sentences.en: We've grabbed a couple more of our esteemed colleagues, both culture writers.
sentences.zh: 我们请来了另外两位尊敬的同事，他们都是文化作家。

sentences.en: We've asked each of them to pick their most beloved good, bad movie of all time.
sentences.zh: 我们要求他们每人挑选一部自己最喜爱的、历代最经典的“雷片好片”。

sentences.en: And we'll have some good, bad, low-stakes debate about it.
sentences.zh: 然后我们将围绕它展开一场轻松有趣的、无伤大雅的辩论。

sentences.en: Let's do that.
sentences.zh: 我们开始吧。

sentences.en: That sounds so fun.
sentences.zh: 听起来太有趣了。

sentences.en: I'm Winnalou.
sentences.zh: 我是Winnalou。

sentences.en: I write the game Connections, one of the puzzles from New York Times games.
sentences.zh: 我负责编写《纽约时报》游戏板块的纵横连线（Connections）谜题。

sentences.en: And I love horror movies.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢恐怖片。

sentences.en: I love my dog.
sentences.zh: 我爱我的狗。

sentences.en: And I love trying to trick you.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢尝试捉弄你们。

sentences.en: I'm Sam Mazursky, and I create the game Spelling Bee and Letterboxd on a daily basis.
sentences.zh: 我是Sam Mazursky，我每天负责制作拼字蜜蜂（Spelling Bee）和Letterboxd游戏。

sentences.en: And I have this thing called promesthesia.
sentences.zh: 我有一种叫做“彩色联觉”的奇特感知。

sentences.en: I see color when I'm listening to music.
sentences.zh: 当我听音乐时我能看到颜色。

sentences.en: New York Times games are made by people, like the ones you just heard from.
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》的游戏是由真人制作的，就像你刚刚听到声音的那些人一样。

sentences.en: Go to nytimes.com slash games to start playing today.
sentences.zh: 访问nytimes.com/games今天就开始游玩吧。

sentences.en: Okay, we are back.
sentences.zh: 好了，我们回来了。

sentences.en: Maya, welcome back.
sentences.zh: 玛雅，欢迎回来。

sentences.en: I have assembled all of you here today for a low-stakes debate.
sentences.zh: 我今天把大家聚在这里，进行一场低风险的辩论。

sentences.en: We have Maya Salam.
sentences.zh: 我们有玛雅·萨拉姆。

sentences.en: Ready to fight playfully.
sentences.zh: 随时准备好开玩笑地切磋一番。

sentences.en: I've also got Gilbert Cruz, the Times' new Canon editor, which means that Gilbert is in charge of thinking about great books, great TV shows, great movies,
sentences.zh: 我们还有吉尔伯特·克鲁兹，他是《时报》的新任经典编辑，这意味着吉尔伯特负责思考伟大的书籍、伟大的电视剧、伟大的电影，

sentences.en: also former books and culture editor.
sentences.zh: 他也是前图书与文化编辑。

sentences.en: Rachel, thanks for having me.
sentences.zh: 雷切尔，谢谢邀请我来。

sentences.en: And we have Taffy Brodesser-Akner, a novelist and a writer for the Times Magazine.
sentences.zh: 我们还有塔菲·布罗德瑟-阿克纳，她是小说家兼《时报杂志》的撰稿人。

sentences.en: Taffy, thank you for being here.
sentences.zh: 塔菲，谢谢你来到这里。

sentences.en: It's great to be here.
sentences.zh: 很高兴来到这里。

sentences.en: Thank you for having me.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你们邀请我。

sentences.en: How's everybody feeling today?
sentences.zh: 大家今天感觉怎么样？

sentences.en: Good, bad?
sentences.zh: 好，还是不好？

sentences.en: Great.
sentences.zh: 太棒了。

sentences.en: I'm confused by you calling it low-stakes.
sentences.zh: 你管这叫低风险，我可被你搞糊涂了。

sentences.en: I agree.
sentences.zh: 我同意。

sentences.en: This is pretty high-stakes.
sentences.zh: 这风险可挺高的。

sentences.en: Okay, okay.
sentences.zh: 好吧，好吧。

sentences.en: Maya, you're the one that came up with the low-stakes debate idea.
sentences.zh: 玛雅，提出“低风险辩论”这个主意的人可是你。

sentences.en: Do you want to explain?
sentences.zh: 你要不要解释一下？

sentences.en: What I mean about that is what makes a lot of these good, bad movies fun is that
sentences.zh: 我这么说意思是，很多这类“雷片好片”之所以有趣，是因为

sentences.en: they are meant to be watched and to be bantered about, to have funny comments, to watch not so quietly.
sentences.zh: 它们就是用来观看和吐槽的，可以爆发出好笑的评论，而且看的时候很难保持安静。

sentences.en: Taffy, does that satisfy your question?
sentences.zh: 塔菲，这能解答你的疑问吗？

sentences.en: I guess so.
sentences.zh: 我想是的吧。

sentences.en: Reasonable people can disagree.
sentences.zh: 理性的人总是可以有不同意见的。

sentences.en: I think the thing with Taffy is it's impossible for her to ever talk about movies in a low-stakes way, even if she's talking about a good, bad movie, a good movie, a bad movie.
sentences.zh: 我觉得塔菲这个人，她根本不可能以一种低风险的方式去谈论电影，哪怕她谈的是一部“雷片好片”、一部好电影或者一部烂电影。

sentences.en: Well, that is slightly terrifying because...
sentences.zh: 嗯，这稍微有点吓人，因为……

sentences.en: Okay, okay.
sentences.zh: 好吧，好吧。

sentences.en: Gilbert and Taffy, you are both movie lovers.
sentences.zh: 吉尔伯特和塔菲，你们俩都是影迷。

sentences.en: Are you good, bad movie lovers?
sentences.zh: 你们也是“雷片好片”的影迷吗？

sentences.en: Are they part of your diet?
sentences.zh: 这类电影也在你们的观影库里吗？

sentences.en: Is this a topic that you have thought about before?
sentences.zh: 这是你们以前思考过的话题吗？

sentences.en: Taffy, let's start with you.
sentences.zh: 塔菲，我们从你开始吧。

sentences.en: I mean, I feel I have been fighting my whole life to say that if it's good, it's good.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我觉得我一生都在抗争，想要证明只要它是好的，那就是好的。

sentences.en: And it doesn't matter what its provenance or its vintage is.
sentences.zh: 它的出身或年代并不重要。

sentences.en: And it doesn't matter...
sentences.zh: 这都无所谓……

sentences.en: I don't care where a movie went to school.
sentences.zh: 我才不管一部电影是在哪所学校毕业的（出身背景如何）。

sentences.en: I care that it made me feel something and that it's memorable and that it sort of changes my metabolism and that it locks me in.
sentences.zh: 我关心的它是否能让我有所触动，它是否让人难忘，它是否能改变我的新陈代谢并让我全神贯注。

sentences.en: You don't care that a movie had a good pedigree.
sentences.zh: 你并不在乎一部电影是否拥有良好的血统。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Gilbert, would you agree with that?
sentences.zh: 吉尔伯特，你同意这一点吗？

sentences.en: Not really.
sentences.zh: 其实不然。

sentences.en: I think there are good things in this world.
sentences.zh: 我认为这个世界上有好东西。

sentences.en: I think there are bad things in this world.
sentences.zh: 我认为这个世界上也有坏东西。

sentences.en: I think there are good movies and there are bad movies.
sentences.zh: 我认为有好的电影，也有烂的电影。

sentences.en: The way in which those two things come together in the good, bad movie is...
sentences.zh: 这两种特质在“雷片好片”中结合的方式是……

sentences.en: It's something, I think, to Maya's point, that you find yourself drawn to again and again, even as you're able to identify parts of it that are bad.
sentences.zh: 我觉得，正如玛雅所说，哪怕你能看出它不好的地方，你还是会发现自己一次又一次地被它吸引。

sentences.en: Whether it's the script or the cinematography or the music or various performances can be genuinely bad, in my opinion.
sentences.zh: 在我看来，无论是剧本、摄影、音乐还是各种表演，都可能会真的很烂。

sentences.en: However, those are balanced out by other parts of the movie that are so compelling to you that you find yourself, whether because of nostalgia reasons or what have you,
sentences.zh: 然而，这些缺点会被电影中其他极具吸引力的部分所平衡，让你不知不觉中——无论是出于怀旧的原因还是别的什么——

sentences.en: watching something over and over again.
sentences.zh: 一遍又一遍地看这部作品。

sentences.en: There are many movies that I love and I love them because I think they're genuinely good.
sentences.zh: 有很多我喜爱的电影，我爱它们是因为我认为它们本身就真的很好。

sentences.en: However, some of the movies we're going to talk about today are in a different category.
sentences.zh: 然而，我们今天将要讨论的一些电影属于不同的类别。

sentences.en: I think it's okay for them to be in a different category.
sentences.zh: 我觉得它们属于不同的类别也没问题。

sentences.en: You guys are making the distinction, this sort of distinction as old as Hollywood itself, between a movie that is good because we can appreciate that it is good on paper,
sentences.zh: 你们在做出这种区分——这种和好莱坞本身一样古老的区分——一边是那种我们在纸面上就能欣赏它的好、它在电影层面上很好、它是……

sentences.en: it is cinematically good, it is...
sentences.zh: 你能看出它的制作工艺之精良的电影；

sentences.en: you can see the craft, and a movie that is good because you like it.
sentences.zh: 另一边是那种因为你喜欢它而觉得好的电影。

sentences.en: Are we allowed to call movies good just because they are enjoyable and perhaps even popular?
sentences.zh: 我们是否可以仅仅因为一部电影具有观赏性甚至可能很受欢迎，就称它为好电影？

sentences.en: I say yes, but it seems like Gilbert says no.
sentences.zh: 我说可以，但吉尔伯特似乎说不可以。

sentences.en: I think, Taffy, if I said to you, what is the difference between Michael Clayton, one of your favorite movies, which is a good movie, capital G, good movie,
sentences.zh: 塔菲，我想如果我问你，你的最爱之一《全面毁灭》（Michael Clayton）——这是一部大写“G”的好电影——

sentences.en: and one or two of the movies that you're going to talk about in a few minutes, I think you would put them in different categories, perhaps.
sentences.zh: 和你等会儿要谈的一两部电影之间有什么区别，我想你可能会把它们归入不同的类别。

sentences.en: You know what?
sentences.zh: 你知道吗？

sentences.en: That's a very good question.
sentences.zh: 这真是个好问题。

sentences.en: When we started talking about this, I was thinking, again, about the provenance of even the discussion, and I wondered how everybody else chose their movies,
sentences.zh: 当我们开始讨论这个话题时，我其实又在思考这场讨论本身的来源，我在想其他人都是怎么挑选他们的电影的，

sentences.en: since in the vast canon, lowercase c, of movies, to me, this was a crushing assignment.
sentences.zh: 因为在广袤的电影正典（小写c）中，对我来说，这是一个令人抓狂的任务。

sentences.en: You're raising a good point, which is we should talk about the criteria that you guys are using to define good-bad.
sentences.zh: 你提出了一点，那就是我们应该讨论你们用来定义“雷片好片”的标准。

sentences.en: And, Maya, since this is your project, you want to...
sentences.zh: 而且，玛雅，既然这是你的项目，你想……

sentences.en: let's run your theory of the case by Gilbert and Taffy and see what they think.
sentences.zh: 让我们拿你的理论让吉尔伯特和塔菲品评一下，看看他们怎么想。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: And there are no wrong answers to this question, in my opinion.
sentences.zh: 在我看来，这个问题没有标准答案。

sentences.en: We'll tell you if that's true.
sentences.zh: 到时候我们就知道是不是这样了。

sentences.en: We'll see about that.
sentences.zh: 我们拭目以待。

sentences.en: And I do think this conversation about the philosophy of what good means, what bad means, and what good-bad means, this is really the point,
sentences.zh: 而且我确实认为，关于“好”意味着什么、“坏”意味着什么、以及“雷片好片”意味着什么的哲学探讨，这才是真正的核心，

sentences.en: the conversation that's happening right now.
sentences.zh: 也就是我们现在正在进行的对话。

sentences.en: So, while they are called good-bad, and the way that we break it down is, what makes this movie good?
sentences.zh: 所以，虽然它们被称为“雷片好片”，我们的拆解方式是：是什么让这部电影好？

sentences.en: It's actual, redeemable qualities.
sentences.zh: 是它实际存在的、可取 Qualities（品质）。

sentences.en: What makes it bad?
sentences.zh: 是什么让它变坏？

sentences.en: It's irredeemable qualities.
sentences.zh: 是它不可救药的品质。

sentences.en: And what makes it good-bad, which is the silly, the fun, the completely over-the-top, you know, maybe it's the corny special effects, the cringy puns, the overacting.
sentences.zh: 而是什么让它成为了“雷片好片”呢？就是那些傻气的、好玩的、完全夸张的元素，你知道的，也许是俗气的特效、令人脚趾抠的谐音梗、过度的表演。

sentences.en: It gets to a point where they all loop back into virtues and make the movie what it is.
sentences.zh: 它们发展到一定程度，就会反过来变成优点，造就了这部电影独特的魅力。

sentences.en: Gilbert, canon editor, what do you think?
sentences.zh: 吉尔伯特，经典编辑，你怎么看？

sentences.en: I, you know, I agree more with Maya than I disagree.
sentences.zh: 我，你知道的，我同意玛雅的成分多过反对。

sentences.en: I mean, I recently was on vacation and we threw on Point Break because the end of the film was filmed near where we were vacationing in Oregon.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我最近去度假时，我们重温了《惊爆点》（Point Break），因为电影结尾是在我们在俄勒冈州度假的附近取景的。

sentences.en: And I love that movie.
sentences.zh: 我很喜欢那部电影。

sentences.en: I've seen it many times.
sentences.zh: 我已经看过很多遍了。

sentences.en: It has some of the best action scenes that were filmed in the 90s.
sentences.zh: 它拥有90年代拍摄的一些最棒的动作场面。

sentences.en: And then you have Keanu Reeves' line deliveries that are not good.
sentences.zh: 然后你又会听到基努·里维斯那些实在算不上好的台词交付。

sentences.en: You cannot look at Keanu Reeves saying, I am FBI agent!
sentences.zh: 你看着基努·里维斯说“我是FBI探员！”

sentences.en: I know, man.
sentences.zh: “我知道，老兄。”

sentences.en: And feel like that was the right take.
sentences.zh: 你绝不会觉得那是对一条正确的表演处理。

sentences.en: Like, surely there were a couple more takes.
sentences.zh: 就像是，导演肯定拍了好几个备选条目吧。

sentences.en: Yet, the movie is eminently rewatchable, quite amazing in certain parts, even though there are these elements that you can identify as just not great.
sentences.zh: 然而，这部电影极其耐看，在某些部分相当惊艳，尽管其中确实存在一些你一眼就能看出“实在不咋地”的元素。

sentences.en: I can watch a great movie, a Chinatown, a There Will Be Blood, and say, actually, no notes.
sentences.zh: 我可以看一部伟大的电影，比如《唐人街》、《血色将至》，然后说：真的，无可挑剔。

sentences.en: I don't see a lot that I would quibble with.
sentences.zh: 我挑不出什么毛病。

sentences.en: Go with God.
sentences.zh: 走好不送。

sentences.en: But you can always find something in a good, bad movie that you can make fun of.
sentences.zh: 但你总能在一部“雷片好片”里找到你可以拿来开玩笑的点。

sentences.en: And when you're watching it in the group, everyone laughs at the same time because it's so dumb.
sentences.zh: 当你和大家一起看的时候，所有人都会在同一时间笑出来，因为它实在是太蠢了。

sentences.en: Exactly that.
sentences.zh: 完全就是这样。

sentences.en: I think there is something to be teased out about for each individual person, how much their idea of a good, bad movie is attached to nostalgia in some way.
sentences.zh: 我觉得对于每个人来说，都有一点值得细细品味，那就是他们对“雷片好片”的喜爱在多大程度上以某种方式与怀旧情结绑在一起。

sentences.en: I encountered this when I was younger, when I was a teenager, what have you.
sentences.zh: 我年轻时、还是个青少年的时候，诸如此类的时候就遇到过这种事。

sentences.en: I've seen it many, many, many times, whether because, for those of a certain age, it was on cable, or I had played the DVD over and over again in college.
sentences.zh: 我已经看过无数次了，无论是对某一特定年龄段的人来说它曾在有线电视上播放，还是我在大学里把这张DVD放了一遍又一遍。
